mathcs.title: Mathematics for Computer Science
mathcs.description: Build the proof, counting, probability, and linear algebra skills that sit underneath algorithms, cryptography, graphics, and machine learning.
mathcs.audience: For learners who want the mathematical depth of a university computer science degree.
mathcs.goal: Read and write rigorous arguments and apply discrete math, probability, calculus, and linear algebra to computing problems.

relatedTracks.reason: Data structures, algorithms, and theory of computation
Proof and counting skills applied to algorithm analysis
Linear algebra, calculus, and probability behind machine learning

levels.goal: Write correct proofs and count possibilities systematically.

skills.name: Proof Techniques & Induction
skills.description: Prove statements using direct proof, contradiction, and mathematical induction.
outcomes: Choose between direct proof, contradiction, and contrapositive
Prove properties of recursive programs by induction
Spot gaps and errors in an informal argument

resources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.042J: Mathematics for Computer Science
Book of Proof (Richard Hammack): free textbook
Stanford CS103: Mathematical Foundations of Computing
Lean: Natural Number Game - learn proofs interactively
YouTube search: MIT 6.042 proofs and induction lecture
YouTube search: how to write a proof by contradiction

skills.description: Count arrangements and subsets and reason about how many cases an algorithm must handle.
outcomes: Apply the sum and product rules, permutations, and combinations
Use inclusion-exclusion and the pigeonhole principle
Solve simple recurrences that describe counting problems

levels.goal: Model networks, uncertainty, and change with mathematics.

algorithms-adv.title: Advanced Algorithms & Data Structures
algorithms-adv.description: Go beyond sorting and searching with dynamic programming, advanced data structures, graph algorithms, randomization, and intractability.
algorithms-adv.audience: For learners who have finished core data structures and algorithms and want university-level depth.
algorithms-adv.goal: Design, analyze, and implement efficient algorithms and recognize problems that are provably hard.

relatedTracks.reason: Core data structures, algorithm design, and complexity
Proofs, counting, and probability used in analysis

levels.goal: Solve problems by reusing subproblems and making locally optimal choices.

infotheory.title: Information Theory & Advanced Theory
infotheory.description: Learn how information is measured, compressed, protected from errors, and secured, and how geometric problems are solved.
infotheory.audience: For learners who want the theory behind compression, error correction, cryptography, and computational geometry.
infotheory.goal: Reason quantitatively about information and apply coding, security, and geometric algorithms.

relatedTracks.reason: Probability, linear algebra, and number theory
Error detection and correction in communication

levels.goal: Measure information and use it to compress data.
